Table 1 Comparison of the optimal gate error rates for the SC and the cat. All errors are normalized by the optimal gate errors of the cat, which are given by \({p}_{Z(\theta )}=\frac{\theta }{2}\sqrt{\frac{1}{\bar{n}}\frac{{\kappa }_{1}}{{\kappa }_{2}}}\) and \({p}_{{{{\rm{CNOT}}}}}=\frac{\pi }{2\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{\frac{{\kappa }_{1}}{{\kappa }_{2}}}\)58. The definitions of \(\hat{F}\) and \({\hat{F}}^{{\prime} }\) are given in Eq. (7) and Eq. (15) respectively. The optimal gate errors for SC are reached at \(\eta \approx \frac{1}{2}\). The optima Z(θ) gate time for SC with \({\hat{F}}^{{\prime} }\) and \(\hat{F}\) are approximately \(\frac{\pi }{4\sqrt{{\kappa }_{1}{\kappa }_{2}}}{\bar{n}}^{-5/2}\) and \(\frac{\pi }{4\sqrt{3{\kappa }_{1}{\kappa }_{2}}}{\bar{n}}^{-7/2}\) respectively. The gate times for CNOT are approximately \(\frac{\pi }{4\sqrt{2{\kappa }_{1}{\kappa }_{2}}}{\bar{n}}^{-3/2}\) and \(\frac{\pi }{12\sqrt{{\kappa }_{1}{\kappa }_{2}}}{\bar{n}}^{-5/2}\) respectively. Since the cooling time is mostly assumed to be constant in our gate scheme, it is neglected for simplicity. We only provide the scaling of the gate errors with \(\bar{n}\) for the SC since the exact expressions are complicated, as shown in Methods.
